claims.text: Machine-learning models trained on historical data can harm protected groups through incorrect predictions or withholding of resources.
Principles of distributive justice must be incorporated into machine learning model design, deployment, and evaluation to advance health equity.
Technical implementations of distributive justice in healthcare machine learning can target equality in patient outcomes.
Technical implementations of distributive justice in healthcare machine learning can target equality in model performance.
Technical implementations of distributive justice in healthcare machine learning can target equality in resource allocation.

evidence.description: Because machine-learning models learn from historically collected data, populations that have experienced human and structural biases in the past-called protected groups-are vulnerable to harm by incorrect predictions or withholding of resources.
For that goal to be achieved, principles of distributive justice must be incorporated into model design, deployment, and evaluation.
The article describes several technical implementations of distributive justice-specifically those that ensure equality in patient outcomes...
The article describes several technical implementations of distributive justice-specifically those that ensure equality in... performance...
The article describes several technical implementations of distributive justice-specifically those that ensure equality in... resource allocation...

methodologies.name: Distributive Justice Framework for Clinical ML
methodologies.description: A framework mapping principles of distributive justice to clinical machine learning design, deployment, and evaluation criteria.

limitations.text: Machine-learning models learn from historically collected data that reflect past human and structural biases.

future_work.text: Encode principles of justice into clinical decision support and population-level monitoring models to ensure they benefit all patients.
